raw_case_text:
A 39-year-old female presented with complaints of generalized abdominal distension, weight loss, swelling of legs, and muscle weakness extant for several weeks. Her past medical history was significant for a well-controlled HIV infection of 6 years on highly active anti-retroviral therapy, hypertension, ESRD secondary to HIV-associated nephropathy, and secondary hyperparathyroidism. She was a non-smoker and had no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Her initial renal biopsy revealed collapsing focal glomerular sclerosis, microcystic dilation of renal tubules, lymphocytic interstitial infiltrates, and interstitial fibrosis. She received chronic cycler-assisted peritoneal dialysis (PD) for 5 years and was well controlled clinically regarding uremic and volume status with no abnormalities regarding color, viscosity, or volume of exchanges. Subsequently, she was transitioned to intermittent hemodialysis (HD) due to personal preferences. A few weeks after the transition to intermittent HD, ascites of unclear etiology developed, ultimately requiring repeated large-volume paracentesis with ~ 5 - 7 L ascitic fluid removals every other week. 
There were no associated symptoms of coughing, palpitations, or shortness of breath. She was chronically anuric. Vital signs showed blood pressure of 160/80 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats/min (regular), respiratory rate 16/min and temperature 36.9  C. Oxygen saturation was 98% on ambient room air. Her physical examination was remarkable for moderate ascites and edema of the lower extremities. Otherwise neurological, respiratory, and cardiovascular examinations were normal without organomegaly and without clinical stigmata or symptoms of chronic liver disease or heart failure. 
Laboratory investigations showed normocytic, normochromic anemia with a hemoglobin of 10 g/dL and uncorrected serum calcium of 8.6 mg/dL. Other labs were as follows: CD4 T-cell count: 600/mm3, HIV viral load: 986 copies/mL (reference: < 40 copies/mL), serum creatinine: 10.3 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase: 13 U/L (normal range: 5 - 34 U/L), alanine aminotransferase: 17 U/L (5 - 45 U/L), bilirubin: 0.4 mg/dL, prothrombin time INR: 1.01, serum albumin: 2.3 mg/dL, serum amylase: 105 IU/L (27 - 130 U/L), serum lipase: 40 IU/L (8 - 78 U/L). Her tumor antigens (Ag) were within reference range for cancer antigen (CA) 15-3 and CA19-9. CA 125 levels were repeatedly elevated (197 - 416 U/mL (normal: < 34.9 U/mL)), but no further follow-up was obtained. Analysis of the ascites fluid showed an albumin level of 1.5 g/dL and protein of 3.5 g/dL. The serum-to-ascites albumin gradient was < 1.1 excluding portal hypertension as a cause of ascites. The culture of peritoneal fluid was negative for acid-fast bacilli. There were no fungi seen by calcofluor white stain. Histoplasma Ag and Aspergillus Ag were negative. The pancreas was reported normal on computed tomography. Her beta-2 microglobulin was elevated to 47.30 mg/L (normal: 0.80 - 2.3). Serum protein electrophoresis showed hypoalbuminemia and decreased total protein, with minimal monoclonal M-component only (IgG-kappa 0.30 g/dL in the gamma zone). Immunofixation electrophoresis showed polyclonal immunoglobulins (Ig) with polyclonal light chains. kappa and lambda light chains were increased to 66.86 mg/dL (normal: 0.33 - 1.94) and 18.55 mg/dL (normal: 0.57 - 2.63), respectively, yielding a ratio of 3.6 (normal: 0.26 - 1.65) (Table 1). Ascitic fluid analysis showed a marked increase in plasma cells with an abnormal kappa : lambda ratio, i.e., > 5 : 1. 
Liver biopsy was essentially normal, hence an omental biopsy was performed which on immunohistochemistry showed similar findings as the ascitic fluid with predominant kappa and faint lambda staining (Figure 1). Multiple myeloma work-ups with skeletal surveys revealed no focal osseous lesions, apart from the osseous changes of hyperparathyroidism. Accordingly, the diagnosis of omental EMP with malignant ascites was established. Omental resection and radiation were offered to the patient, but she refused further intervention. Two years of follow-up, she remained stable without any further complication, apart from requiring regular paracenteses.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old female presenting with progressive abdominal distension, bilateral leg swelling, muscle weakness, and weight loss for several weeks.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a multi-week history of worsening painless abdominal distension, bilateral lower extremity edema, proximal muscle weakness, and unintentional weight loss. Several weeks after transitioning from long-term peritoneal dialysis to intermittent hemodialysis, she developed rapid, recurrent, high-volume ascites requiring therapeutic paracentesis of 5 to 7 liters every two weeks.
subjective.past_medical_history: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection diagnosed 6 years prior, maintained on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART); end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to biopsy-proven HIV-associated nephropathy (HIVAN, characterized by collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis), managed with cycler peritoneal dialysis for 5 years before elective transfer to intermittent hemodialysis; hypertension; secondary hyperparathyroidism; chronic anuria. No history of tobacco, alcohol, or illicit substance use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Abdominal distension, peripheral edema, generalized weakness, weight loss; denies dyspnea, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, cough, chest pain, palpitations, or abdominal pain.

objective.physical_examination: Vitals: Blood pressure 160/80 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.9 °C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Abdomen: Prominent abdominal distension with shifting dullness consistent with moderate ascites, soft and non-tender; no hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, or stigmata of chronic liver disease (spider angiomas, palmar erythema). Extremities: Bilateral pitting pedal edema. Cardiovascular and Respiratory: Normal heart sounds without gallop or murmur; clear breath sounds bilaterally.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL (normocytic, normochromic anemia). Comprehensive metabolic panel: Serum creatinine 10.3 mg/dL, serum albumin 2.3 g/dL, uncorrected serum calcium 8.6 mg/dL, total bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL, AST 13 U/L, ALT 17 U/L, serum amylase 105 IU/L, serum lipase 40 IU/L, prothrombin time INR 1.01. Paracentesis / Ascitic fluid: Total protein 3.5 g/dL, albumin 1.5 g/dL, serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) < 1.1 (exudative ascites); calcofluor white fungal stain negative; Histoplasma and Aspergillus antigens negative; acid-fast bacilli (AFB) culture negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Tumor and hematologic biomarkers: CA-125 elevated (197-416 U/mL; reference < 34.9 U/mL), CA 15-3 and CA 19-9 normal; serum beta-2 microglobulin 47.30 mg/L. Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation: Hypoalbuminemia, minimal monoclonal IgG-kappa M-spike (0.30 g/dL in gamma zone); serum free kappa light chains 66.86 mg/dL, lambda 18.55 mg/dL (ratio 3.6). Ascitic fluid cytology: Markedly elevated monoclonal plasma cell infiltrate with kappa:lambda ratio > 5:1. Abdominal CT: Moderate-to-severe ascites with normal pancreas and liver parenchyma. Core needle liver biopsy: Histologically normal liver tissue. Omental biopsy: Sheets of atypical plasma cells with monotypic kappa light chain restriction on immunohistochemistry. Skeletal radiographic survey: Absence of osteolytic lesions (findings limited to hyperparathyroid osteopathy).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Primary omental extramedullary plasmacytoma (EMP) presenting with recurrent malignant ascites, in a patient with well-controlled HIV infection (CD4 count 600/mm3, HIV viral load 986 copies/mL) and ESRD on maintenance hemodialysis; peritoneal tuberculosis, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, ovarian malignancy, cirrhosis, and systemic multiple myeloma were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Offered definitive surgical omental resection and adjuvant radiotherapy, which the patient declined. Managed conservatively with continued HAART, maintenance hemodialysis, and serial therapeutic paracenteses (5-7 L evacuated every other week). Remained clinically stable without disease progression over two years of follow-up.
